read.sections.0.text.source:
A mountain landscape can contain engineering as well as trees and soil. In Ifugao province, in the northern Philippines, stepped rice fields show how people have shaped slopes for farming. A cultural landscape is a place shaped by the links between people and their surroundings. Ifugao includes different Indigenous communities and languages, among them Tuwali, Ayangan and Kalanguya. Their landscapes and buildings do not stand for every community in the Philippines. Differences between places matter as much as the knowledge they share.

Terrace builders make level pond fields along the curves of the mountain. A terrace is a level field made on a slope. Stone or earth walls hold up the fields, while a network of irrigation carries water from the forest on the heights. Irrigation means bringing water to farmland through a managed system. The shape of the land, the strength of a wall and the movement of water are linked engineering problems. So a terrace's curved outline records decisions about growing food on steep ground. It is not simply a pretty pattern.
read.sections.0.text.back:
A mountain landscape can contain engineering besides trees and soil. In Ifugao province, in the north of the Philippines, terraced rice fields show how people have shaped slopes for farming. A cultural landscape is a place shaped by the links between people and their surroundings. Ifugao includes different Indigenous communities and languages, among them Tuwali, Ayangan and Kalanguya. Their landscapes and buildings do not stand for every community in the Philippines. Differences between places are as important as the knowledge that is shared.

Terrace builders make level fields that hold water, following the curves of the mountain. A terrace is a level plot of land made on a hillside. Stone or earth walls hold up the fields, while a network of irrigation brings water from the forest on the high ground. Irrigation means bringing water to farmland through a managed system. The shape of the land, the strength of a wall and the flow of water are engineering problems linked to each other. So the curved outline of a terrace records decisions about growing food on steep ground. It is not merely a pretty pattern.
read.sections.0.text.note: "Indigenous" is "Orang Asal", the term Malaysia uses for Indigenous peoples in general ("Orang Asli" means the Peninsular groups only); reviewer to confirm it suits communities in the Philippines. "Irrigation" is "pengairan".

read.sections.0.simpler.source:
Mountains can hold clever building work, not just trees and soil. Ifugao is in the north of the Philippines. There, people shaped steep hills into rice fields. This is a cultural landscape. It is a place shaped by people and nature together. Ifugao has different Indigenous groups. Their languages include Tuwali, Ayangan and Kalanguya. They do not stand for every group in the Philippines.

A terrace is a flat field built on a slope. Builders follow the curve of the mountain. Walls of stone or earth hold each field up. Irrigation brings water to the fields. Here, it comes down from the woods above. The land, the walls and the water all work together. So the curved shapes are not just pretty. They show how people grow food on steep land.
read.sections.0.simpler.back:
Mountains can contain clever building work, not only trees and soil. Ifugao is in the north of the Philippines. There, people shaped steep hills into rice fields. This is a cultural landscape. It is a place shaped by people and nature together. Ifugao has different Indigenous groups. Their languages include Tuwali, Ayangan and Kalanguya. They do not stand for every group in the Philippines.

A terrace is a flat plot of land built on a hillside. Builders follow the curve of the mountain. Walls of stone or earth hold up each plot. Irrigation brings water to the rice fields. Here, the water comes down from the forest above. The land, the walls and the water all work together. So the curved shapes are not merely pretty. They show the way people grow food on steep land.

read.sections.1.text.source:
The work goes on after the building is done. Fields, walls and water systems need care. UNESCO describes shared upkeep alongside each household owning its own terraces, protected by ancestral rights and customary practices. Customary means guided by a community's established practices and rules. Shared work does not mean that every field belongs to everyone. It means that households depend on links beyond their own plots. Knowledge about planting, protecting the soil and managing water must stay useful across generations.

The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) describes the wider farming system as linked woodland, fields, villages and water. Small woods above the terraces help control the water that reaches the fields. Rice is only part of people's livelihood, the work and resources through which they meet their needs. Vegetables, fish and other foods also matter, and carving and weaving can bring in money. Customary rules help share out duties towards land, water and woods. The landscape joins practical knowledge, family duties and community decisions. Its survival depends on people earning a living as well as on looking after walls.
read.sections.1.text.back:
The work continues after the building is finished. Fields, walls and water systems need care. UNESCO describes shared upkeep alongside each household owning its own terraces, protected by ancestral rights and customary practices. Custom (adat) means a community's practices and rules that have long been accepted and guide life. Shared work does not mean every field belongs to everyone. It means households depend on links outside their own plots. Knowledge about planting, protecting the soil and managing water must stay useful across generations.

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) describes the wider farming system as forest, fields, villages and water linked to each other. Small forests above the terraces help control the water that reaches the fields. Rice is only part of the livelihood of the people there, that is the work and resources they use to meet their needs. Vegetables, fish and other foods are also important, and carving and weaving can bring in money. Customary rules help divide duties towards land, water and forest. This landscape combines practical knowledge, family responsibilities and community decisions. Its survival depends on people being able to earn a living, and not only on looking after the walls.
read.sections.1.text.note: "Customary" (an adjective in English) is the noun "adat" in Malay: "amalan adat", "peraturan adat". "Livelihood" is "mata pencarian".

read.sections.1.simpler.source:
The work goes on after building. Walls and water paths need to be fixed. UNESCO says each family owns its own terraces. Their rights come from their ancestors and from customary rules. Customary means following a group's old rules and ways. But families also work as a team to care for the land. Each family needs its neighbours. People pass on what they know about seeds, soil and water.

The FAO is a world group for food and farms. It says the woods, fields, homes and water all link up. Trees above the terraces help control the water. Rice is only part of people's livelihood. A livelihood is how people get what they need. People also grow beans and greens, and eat fish. Carving and weaving bring in money. The group's rules share out the jobs. To keep the landscape, people must be able to earn a living.
read.sections.1.simpler.back:
The work continues after building. Walls and water paths need to be repaired. UNESCO says each family owns its own terraces. Their rights come from their ancestors and from customary rules. Custom (adat) means a group's old rules and ways. But families also work as one team to look after the land. Each family needs its neighbours. People pass on what they know about seeds, soil and water.

The FAO is a world organisation for food and farming. It says the forest, rice fields, homes and water are all linked. Trees above the terraces help control the water. Rice is only part of the livelihood of the people there. A livelihood is the way people get what they need. People also grow beans and vegetables, and eat fish. Carving and weaving bring in money. That group's rules divide the jobs. To keep that landscape, people must be able to earn a living.

read.sections.2.text.source:
House building belongs to this wider setting. The National Museum of the Philippines describes an Ayangan house from Mayoyao. It has four hardwood posts, a steep grass roof and timber parts fitted together without iron nails. Its single main room served several household tasks, and rice could be stored in the attic. The shaded space below could be used for activities including community rituals. The museum also describes smaller granaries, or rice stores, beside some houses. These uses connect carpentry, food storage, family life and belief. This house type is one example among the varied building traditions of Ifugao.

Such places are living heritage. The FAO names damage to the environment, and how hard it is to earn enough from farming, as threats to this farming system. A beautiful photograph captures one moment. It cannot show every working link or household decision. So caring for the landscape means supporting the people who use and reshape it, as well as respecting their knowledge. It lasts through choices and work that go on, not because a community stays the same.
read.sections.2.text.back:
House building is part of this wider setting. The National Museum of the Philippines describes an Ayangan house from Mayoyao. That house has four hardwood posts, a steep grass roof and wooden parts fitted together without iron nails. Its one main room was used for several household tasks, and rice could be stored in the attic. The shaded space beneath it could be used for various activities, including community ceremonies. The museum also describes smaller granaries, that is places to store rice, beside some houses. These uses connect woodworking, food storage, family life and belief. This type of house is one example among the varied building traditions in Ifugao.

Places like this are living heritage. The FAO names damage to the environment, and how difficult it is to get enough income from farming, as threats to this farming system. A beautiful photograph captures one moment. It cannot show every work connection or household decision. So looking after this landscape means supporting the people who use and reshape it, besides respecting their knowledge. It lasts through choices and work that continue, not because a community stays the same.

read.sections.2.simpler.source:
Houses are part of this landscape too. The National Museum of the Philippines describes an Ayangan house from Mayoyao. It has four strong wooden posts and a steep grass roof. Its wooden parts fit together without iron nails. One main room was used for many jobs at home. Rice could be stored in the space under the roof. The shady space below could be used for group rituals and other things. Some houses had small rice stores next to them. This is one kind of house. Ifugao has many ways of building.

This is living heritage. The FAO says the land is being harmed. It is also hard to earn enough from farming. A photo shows one moment. It cannot show the work and choices of each family. So caring for this place means helping the people who live and work there. The old ways go on because people keep working and choosing.
read.sections.2.simpler.back:
Houses are also part of this landscape. The National Museum of the Philippines describes an Ayangan house from Mayoyao. It has four strong wooden posts and a steep grass roof. Its wooden parts are fitted together without iron nails. One main room was used for many jobs at home. Rice could be stored in the space under the roof. The shady space under the house could be used for group ceremonies and other things. Some houses had small rice stores beside them. This is one kind of house. Ifugao has many ways of building.

This is living heritage. The FAO says the land is being damaged. It is also difficult to get enough income from farming. A photograph shows one moment. It cannot show the work and choices of each family. So looking after this place means helping the people who live and work there. The old ways continue because people keep working and making choices.

write.prompt.source: Explain one link between a built thing and community life. Pick a terrace wall, a water channel or a house's rice store. Use one fact from the reading. Two or three sentences are enough.
write.prompt.back: Explain one connection between something built and community life. Choose a terrace wall, a water channel or a granary beside a house. Use one fact from the reading. Two or three sentences are enough.

write.example.source: One built thing is the stone or earth wall that holds up each terrace. The reading says these walls and the water channels need care after they are built. Families work together to look after them, but each family owns its own fields. This links with community life because no family can keep its terraces working alone. The photo shows the walls, but not who fixes them.

sensitiveNotes.0.source: The reading names Indigenous communities, customary rules and community rituals. Teach them as living practices that communities lead. No learner is asked about their own community, beliefs or family, or to perform any practice. Keep the FAO's point about income factual; don't describe Ifugao communities as poor or behind.
sensitiveNotes.0.back: This reading names Indigenous communities, customary rules and community ceremonies. Teach all of them as living practices led by those communities. No learner is asked about their own community, beliefs or family, or asked to perform any practice. Keep the FAO's point about income factual; don't describe Ifugao communities as poor or backward.

educatorNotes.0.source: A cultural landscape is neither untouched nature nor proof that its communities live the same way or have stopped changing. Shared upkeep does not mean every field is owned by everyone. Ifugao communities do not stand for every community in the Philippines.
educatorNotes.0.back: A cultural landscape is not untouched nature and also not proof that its communities live the same way or have stopped changing. Shared upkeep does not mean every field is owned by everyone. Ifugao communities do not stand for every community in the Philippines.

educatorNotes.1.source: Answer points for Write: retaining walls and level fields linked to food and continuing upkeep; irrigation linked to woodland, water management and cooperation; or the house's attic or granary linked to rice storage and the household's livelihood. Accept other links the reading supports. Learners should not infer ownership, beliefs or a terrace's age from how it looks.
educatorNotes.1.back: Answer points for Write: retaining walls and level plots connected with food and continuing upkeep; irrigation connected with forest, water management and cooperation; or the house's attic or granary connected with rice storage and the household's livelihood. educatorNotes.2.source: UNESCO's page for property 722 (retrieved 7 November 2026) supports the place, the engineering, upkeep, ancestral ownership and changing conditions. The lesson does not adopt its "2,000 years" or "virtually unchanged" wording, and the World Heritage listing covers five named clusters, not every rice terrace in the Philippines.
educatorNotes.2.back: UNESCO's page for heritage property 722 (retrieved on 7 November 2026) supports the place, the engineering, upkeep, ancestral ownership and the changing conditions. This lesson does not use the words "2,000 years" or "virtually unchanged" from that page, and the World Heritage listing covers five named clusters, not every terraced rice field in the Philippines.

educatorNotes.3.source: The FAO profile supports the linked land uses, woodlots, food, extra income and customary management; its undated poverty ranking is left out. The 2024 Tentative List submission names the Tuwali, Ayangan and Kalanguya communities; it is a proposal by the state, not an inscription. No claims are made about the Hudhud chants, and no video is needed for this lesson.
